overview: This Senate resolution congratulates the students, families, teachers, and leaders of public charter schools and supports the goals of the 27th annual National Charter Schools Week, held May 10 through 16, 2026. Charter schools are tuition-free public schools that run with more independence than traditional public schools in exchange for being held accountable for results by an approving body, and they often admit students by lottery when there are more applicants than seats. The resolution credits charter schools with helping close achievement gaps, especially for disadvantaged students, and encourages Americans to hold events showing support for high-quality charter schools. It is symbolic and does not change any law or funding. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on June 9, 2026.
for: Supporters say charter schools give families more public school options and are held accountable for results, and that recognizing their students and teachers is appropriate.
against: Critics say the resolution presents only the favorable side of a debated education policy, and it is symbolic, changing no law or funding.
